subject: Physics
q: Bodies A and B each have mass 0.1 kg. Initially, A moves with velocity 3i m/s and B with velocity 5j m/s. They collide elastically, after which A moves with velocity 4(i + j) m/s. If the kinetic energy of B after the collision is x/10 J, find x.
hint: Use vector conservation of momentum to find B's final velocity.
solution: For equal masses, momentum conservation gives v_B = (3i + 5j) - 4(i + j) = -i + j m/s. Thus |v_B|² = 2 and K_B = (1/2)(0.1)(2) = 0.1 J = x/10 J, so x = 1. The total final kinetic energy is also 1.6 + 0.1 = 1.7 J, matching the initial value and confirming the elastic-collision condition.
